digest.component_or_area: structured-output orchestration (RP-01 Pydantic AI seam replacement)
propositions: Rebar's existing structured-output behavior encodes deterministic repair, extraction, truncation, retry limits, provider fallback, usage accounting, and telemetry that must be preserved or explicitly approved as intentional changes before RP-01 migration to Pydantic AI seams.

An offline probe exercising real Pydantic AI 1.107.2 Agent/output/retry/limits/hooks with mocked transport must reproduce 19 declared scenarios and classify each outcome as preserve, intentionally change, or explicit maintainer decision.

The retry-loop ownership decision—whether Pydantic or Rebar controls output-validation retry—is the highest-impact unresolved maintainer choice affecting request budget, three-attempt ceiling, deterministic repair, stop-reason fast-fail, and cumulative usage.

Material behavioral deltas between current Rebar and Pydantic AI 1.107.2 include request-budget semantics, retry-message wire shape, successful-retry usage aggregation, output-exhaustion exception translation, and ProcessHistory response truncation that must be explicitly decided rather than inherited.

Approved decision D1 mandates one operation-wide request_limit shared by tool turns and output retries, sized as base allowance plus bounded retry allowance, with UsageLimitExceeded raised on exhaustion rather than per-attempt budget reset.

Pending maintainer choice D2 is whether to retain the existing 2,000-character retry-prompt projection of failed intermediate responses or intentionally remove truncation and send full response text back to the model.
